name: IL-09
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+19 partisan lean anchors the race firmly in Democratic territory
Biss has raised about $2.9 million with heavy outside spending, while Elleson shows no reported fundraising
Open seat after Schakowsky's retirement adds modest uncertainty without changing the structural advantage
Prediction markets price Democratic win odds near 96 percent
model.rationale: The district's nineteen-point Democratic lean, Biss's overwhelming fundraising advantage over a Republican with no reported financing, and market pricing near 96 percent all point to the seat staying safely Democratic despite the open-seat transition.
model.watch: A wave of late outside spending against Biss or an unforeseen campaign development could narrow the margin, though a Republican upset remains a long shot.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jan Schakowsky (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Illinois's 9th District sits deep in Democratic territory, with a partisan lean of roughly nineteen points, and Jan Schakowsky's retirement hands the seat to a new face rather than testing an incumbent. Daniel Biss enters the general election with about three million dollars raised and substantial outside spending both for and against him, while Republican John Elleson shows no reported fundraising or cash on hand in the available data. Prediction markets put Democratic odds near ninety-six percent.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals, candidate financing, and market pricing. The open seat adds a modest layer of uncertainty, since Biss has not previously run before this exact electorate, but the structural Democratic advantage is large. Expect the district to remain comfortably Democratic in November unless something outside the current evidence intervenes.
